name: NY-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent advantage with no polling or outside spending against her
model.rationale: Malliotakis holds a Republican-leaning Staten Island seat, a huge cash advantage, and incumbency, while DeCillis has raised almost nothing and no polls or outside spending suggest a contest. Markets price her near-certain reelection, so the forecast stays firmly in Republican territory.
model.watch: Any late polling showing DeCillis within single digits or significant Democratic outside spending would signal a real race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis seeks reelection in a Staten Island–based district that leans Republican by about ten points. She has raised $2.75 million and holds $2.77 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Michael DeCillis has raised under $70,000. No public general-election polls exist, and no outside groups are spending meaningfully in the race. Prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 95 percent chance of holding the seat.

With a strong partisan lean, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger lacking financial or external support, the race shows none of the usual warning signs for an upset. The forecast places the expected margin in the mid-teens for Republicans, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling. The seat is rated Safe Republican.
